```{python}
#| label: setup
#| code-fold: true
import os, sys, json, warnings
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "config" / "project.yaml").exists():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT)); os.chdir(ROOT)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib as mpl, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy import stats
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from src.common.data import load_data, load_config

CFG   = load_config()
SEED  = CFG["reproducibility"]["random_seed"]
np.random.seed(SEED)
FIG   = ROOT / "results" / "figures"; FIG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="notebook")
mpl.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "savefig.dpi": 150, "savefig.bbox": "tight",
                     "axes.titlesize": 10, "axes.labelsize": 9,
                     "xtick.labelsize": 8, "ytick.labelsize": 8, "legend.fontsize": 8})

def save(fig, name):
    """Save a figure under results/figures/a02_<name>.png and return the path."""
    p = FIG / f"a02_{name}.png"; fig.savefig(p); return p

def md(obj, **kw):
    """Markdown table from a DataFrame/Series (pandas .to_markdown)."""
    from IPython.display import Markdown
    return Markdown(obj.to_markdown(**kw))

# --- canonical data (ONLY via src/common/data.py) ---------------------------------
df = load_data()

# --- derived columns live in a SEPARATE frame used for the report only ------------
d = df.copy()
d["wy"]     = d.index.year + (d.index.month >= 10).astype(int)   # water year (Oct-Sep)
d["month"]  = d.index.month
d["doy"]    = d.index.dayofyear
d["season"] = pd.Categorical(
    np.select([d.month.isin([12,1,2]), d.month.isin([3,4,5]), d.month.isin([6,7,8])],
              ["DJF","MAM","JJA"], "SON"), ["DJF","MAM","JJA","SON"], ordered=True)

P, PET, Q = d["P"], d["PET"], d["Q"]
Pv, PETv, Qv = P.to_numpy(), PET.to_numpy(), Q.to_numpy()

# --- authoritative period windows (config/project.yaml -> periods.definition) -----
PERDEF = CFG["periods"]["definition"]
PER    = CFG["periods"][PERDEF]
WIN = {
    "evaluation run"      : PER["evaluation"]["run"],
    "evaluation warm-up"  : PER["evaluation"]["warmup"],
    "evaluation metric"   : PER["evaluation"]["metric"],
    "calibration run"     : PER["calibration"]["run"],
    "calibration warm-up" : PER["calibration"]["warmup"],
    "calibration metric"  : PER["calibration"]["metric"],
    "internal train"      : PER["calibration_internal"]["train"],
    "internal validation" : PER["calibration_internal"]["validation"],
}
def win(name):
    a, b = WIN[name]; return d.loc[a:b]

CAL  = win("calibration metric")     # <- the ONLY frame downstream agents may derive stats from
EVAL = win("evaluation metric")      # <- EDA description only (no model quantity derived from it)
KEY  = {}                            # collected key numbers -> handoff
```

# Summary {#sec-summary}

```{python}
#| label: summary-numbers
ann = d.groupby("wy")[["P","PET","Q"]].sum().loc[1949:1988]
KEY["P_mean_mm_yr"]  = float(P.mean()*365.25)
KEY["PET_mean_mm_yr"]= float(PET.mean()*365.25)
KEY["Q_mean_mm_yr"]  = float(Q.mean()*365.25)
KEY["runoff_ratio"]  = float(Q.sum()/P.sum())
KEY["Q_skewness"]    = float(Q.skew())
KEY["pct_zero_P"]    = float(100*(P==0).mean())
print(f"record          : {d.index[0].date()} .. {d.index[-1].date()}  ({len(d)} days = WY1949-WY1988)")
print(f"P   mean        : {P.mean():.3f} mm/d = {P.mean()*365.25:7.1f} mm/yr   (WY range {ann.P.min():.0f}-{ann.P.max():.0f})")
print(f"PET mean        : {PET.mean():.3f} mm/d = {PET.mean()*365.25:7.1f} mm/yr   (WY range {ann.PET.min():.0f}-{ann.PET.max():.0f})")
print(f"Q   mean        : {Q.mean():.3f} mm/d = {Q.mean()*365.25:7.1f} mm/yr   (WY range {ann.Q.min():.0f}-{ann.Q.max():.0f})")
print(f"runoff ratio    : {Q.sum()/P.sum():.3f}   aridity PET/P = {PET.sum()/P.sum():.2f}")
print(f"daily Q skewness: {Q.skew():.2f}   kurtosis {Q.kurtosis():.1f}   Q95/Q5 dynamic range {Q.quantile(.95)/Q.quantile(.05):.0f}x")
```

**Headline findings**

1. The file is **clean**: 14,610 rows, no gaps, no duplicates, no NaN, no negatives, one PET value of exactly
   0.0 mm/d (1966-01-14, physically plausible mid-winter value, not a missing-data code). Q is strictly
   positive (min 0.069 mm/d) — the river is **perennial**, so log/Box-Cox transforms are safe without offsets.
2. **Units are mm/day and the basin area is ~1,950 km²** (@sec-units): the discrete quantum of the Q series
   (0.0012544 mm/d) is exactly 1 ft³/s spread over 1,950 km² (753 mi²), i.e. the series was converted from
   USGS daily-mean discharge in cfs. This matches USGS 02472000 Leaf River near Collins, MS (752 mi²).
3. **The record starts 1948-10-01** — confirmed independently from the PET/P/Q seasonal phase
   (@sec-alignment). This verifies the resolution of ISSUE-001 (`periods.definition: dates`).
4. **PET is *not* a repeated climatology**: same-day-of-year inter-annual SD is 1.30 mm/d against a seasonal
   amplitude of 1.83 mm/d — PET carries real daily weather information (@sec-pet).
5. The catchment is **strongly nonlinear**: event runoff coefficients range 0.004–0.45 over 31 isolated
   events and correlate with antecedent flow (r = 0.57) and event depth (r = 0.60) (@sec-events).
6. **Memory**: recession constant k ≈ 0.90 d⁻¹ (9 d residence time), log-Q ACF e-folding 48 d, and a linear
   P-lag model keeps gaining skill up to ~1 year (R² 0.59 at 10 d → 0.63 at 90 d → 0.65 at 365 d)
   → ≥180-day input sequences for ML models, ≥365-day warm-up for conceptual models (@sec-implications).
7. **The evaluation period is wetter than calibration**: eval-metric mean Q is 1.29× the calibration mean and
   WY1949 is the wettest year of the 40-year record (P rank 1/40) — a genuine extrapolation risk (@sec-periods).

## Integrity checks

```{python}
#| label: tbl-integrity
checks = {}
checks["n rows"]                    = len(df)
checks["expected rows (40 WY)"]     = 40*365 + 10       # 10 leap days 1952..1988
checks["date index continuous"]     = bool((d.index.to_series().diff().dropna() == pd.Timedelta("1D")).all())
checks["duplicate dates"]           = int(d.index.duplicated().sum())
checks["NaN (P/PET/Q)"]             = int(df[["P","PET","Q"]].isna().sum().sum())
checks["negative values"]           = int((df[["P","PET","Q"]] < 0).sum().sum())
checks["exact zeros P"]             = int((P == 0).sum())
checks["exact zeros PET"]           = int((PET == 0).sum())
checks["exact zeros Q"]             = int((Q == 0).sum())
checks["min Q (mm/d)"]              = float(Q.min())
md(pd.Series(checks, name="value").to_frame())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-runs
def const_runs(v):
    g = np.r_[0, (np.diff(v) != 0).cumsum()]
    s = pd.Series(v).groupby(g)
    size, first = s.size(), s.first().to_numpy()
    return size, first

rows = []
for name, v in [("P", Pv), ("PET", PETv), ("Q", Qv)]:
    size, first = const_runs(v)
    nz = size[(size >= 5) & (first > 0)]
    z  = size[(size >= 5) & (first == 0)]
    rows.append(dict(variable=name, longest_run=int(size.max()),
                     runs_ge5_nonzero=int(len(nz)), runs_ge5_zero=int(len(z)),
                     longest_nonzero_run=int(nz.max()) if len(nz) else 0))
runs_tbl = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("variable")
md(runs_tbl)
```

*Constant runs.* P has 556 runs of ≥5 identical values but **all of them are zeros** (dry spells, longest
51 days) — no infill signature. PET never repeats more than twice in a row. Q has 20 runs of ≥5 identical
values (longest 10 days), all at very low flow; these are the fingerprint of USGS reporting discharge to
3 significant figures in cfs during stable recessions, not infilling.

## Units, numeric precision and implied basin area {#sec-units}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-units
qu = np.sort(Q.unique()); dq = np.diff(qu)
quantum = float(np.median(dq[(dq > 0.8*0.001259) & (dq < 1.2*0.001259)]))
CFS = 0.028316846592           # m3/s per ft3/s
area_m2 = CFS*86400*1000/quantum
print(f"distinct Q values                : {len(qu)}")
print(f"modal quantum of the Q series    : {quantum:.7f} mm/d")
print(f"=> basin area if 1 quantum = 1 cfs: {area_m2/1e6:.0f} km2 = {area_m2/1e6/2.58999:.0f} mi2")
print(f"=> Q range in cfs                : {qu[0]/quantum:.0f} .. {qu[-1]/quantum:.0f} cfs")
print(f"P, PET stored to 4 decimals (mm/d); Q to 8 significant digits (conversion artefact)")
print(f"annual P {P.mean()*365.25:.0f} mm/yr, PET {PET.mean()*365.25:.0f} mm/yr, Q {Q.mean()*365.25:.0f} mm/yr"
      f"  -> Q/P = {Q.sum()/P.sum():.3f}")
KEY["implied_area_km2"] = float(area_m2/1e6)
KEY["Q_quantum_mm_d"]   = quantum
```

The mm/day hypothesis is therefore not an assumption but a **measurement**: the Q column is quantised on a
grid whose step equals 1 cfs over 1,950 km², and the resulting annual depths (P ≈ 1,432 mm/yr,
Q ≈ 500 mm/yr) are exactly what is expected for a humid subtropical Gulf-coastal-plain basin in
south Mississippi. Agent 1 should cross-check this 1,950 km² (753 mi²) against the published USGS drainage
area of gauge 02472000 (752 mi²).

# Variable dictionary {#sec-dictionary}

| name | description | units | source | resolution | range (this record) |
|------|-------------|-------|--------|------------|---------------------|
| `P`   | Mean areal precipitation over the basin | mm/day | NWS/USGS gauge network, basin-averaged (classic Leaf River test data set, @duan1992) | daily, 4 decimals | 0 – 221.52 |
| `PET` | Potential evapotranspiration (daily climatic demand) | mm/day | derived (temperature/radiation based), daily varying | daily, 4 decimals | 0 – 9.11 |
| `Q`   | Observed streamflow as depth over the basin | mm/day | USGS daily mean discharge (cfs) / area ≈ 1,950 km² | daily, quantised at 0.00125 mm/d | 0.069 – 64.01 |
| `row` | 0-based file row (added by `src/common/data.py`) | – | – | – | 0 – 14,609 |

Date index: 1948-10-01 … 1988-09-30, daily, complete (water years 1949–1988).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-describe
def describe(s):
    qs = s.quantile([.01,.05,.10,.25,.50,.75,.90,.95,.99,.999])
    out = dict(mean=s.mean(), sd=s.std(), CV=s.std()/s.mean(), skew=s.skew(), kurtosis=s.kurtosis(),
               min=s.min())
    out.update({f"p{q*100:g}": v for q, v in qs.items()})
    out.update(max=s.max(), pct_zero=100*(s == 0).mean())
    return out
DESC = pd.DataFrame({v: describe(d[v]) for v in ["P","PET","Q"]}).T
md(DESC.round(4))
```

*All values in mm/day; `pct_zero` in %; n = 14,610 days.*

# Precipitation P {#sec-p}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-p-stats
wet01, wet1 = P > 0.1, P > 1.0
def spell_lengths(mask):
    out, c = [], 0
    for m in mask:
        if m: c += 1
        elif c: out.append(c); c = 0
    if c: out.append(c)
    return np.array(out)
ws, ds_ = spell_lengths(wet01.to_numpy()), spell_lengths(~wet01.to_numpy())
rx1 = d.groupby("wy")["P"].max().loc[1949:1988]
rx5 = P.rolling(5).sum().groupby(d.wy).max().loc[1949:1988]
mo  = d.groupby(["wy","month"])["P"].sum().unstack()
SI  = (mo.sub(mo.sum(axis=1)/12, axis=0).abs().sum(axis=1)/mo.sum(axis=1)).loc[1949:1988]  # Walsh-Lawler
pstats = {
  "wet-day frequency (>0.1 mm) [%]"   : 100*wet01.mean(),
  "wet-day frequency (>1 mm) [%]"     : 100*wet1.mean(),
  "days >10 mm [%]"                   : 100*(P>10).mean(),
  "days >25 mm [%]"                   : 100*(P>25).mean(),
  "days >50 mm [%]"                   : 100*(P>50).mean(),
  "mean wet-day intensity (>0.1) [mm]": P[wet01].mean(),
  "mean wet-day intensity (>1) [mm]"  : P[wet1].mean(),
  "mean wet spell length [d]"         : ws.mean(),
  "max wet spell length [d]"          : ws.max(),
  "mean dry spell length [d]"         : ds_.mean(),
  "95th pct dry spell [d]"            : np.percentile(ds_, 95),
  "max dry spell length [d]"          : ds_.max(),
  "Rx1day mean / max [mm]"            : rx1.mean(),
  "Rx5day mean / max [mm]"            : rx5.mean(),
  "Walsh-Lawler seasonality index [-]": SI.mean(),
}
print(f"annual P (WY): mean {ann.P.mean():.0f} mm, sd {ann.P.std():.0f} mm, CV {ann.P.std()/ann.P.mean():.2f}, "
      f"min {ann.P.min():.0f} (WY{ann.P.idxmin()}), max {ann.P.max():.0f} (WY{ann.P.idxmax()})")
print(f"Rx1day: mean {rx1.mean():.1f} mm, record max {rx1.max():.1f} mm (WY{rx1.idxmax()});  "
      f"Rx5day: mean {rx5.mean():.1f} mm, max {rx5.max():.1f} mm")
md(pd.Series(pstats, name="value").to_frame().round(3))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-annual
#| fig-cap: "Water-year totals with Theil-Sen trend lines. No significant monotonic trend (Mann-Kendall, see table)."
import pymannkendall as mk
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.2))
mkres = {}
for ax, v, c in zip(axs, ["P","PET","Q"], ["#1f77b4","#d62728","#2ca02c"]):
    r = mk.original_test(ann[v].to_numpy()); mkres[v] = r
    ax.bar(ann.index, ann[v], color=c)
    yy = r.intercept + r.slope*np.arange(len(ann))
    ax.plot(ann.index, yy, "k--", lw=1.2,
            label=f"Sen slope {r.slope:+.1f} mm/yr²\nMK p={r.p:.2f} ({r.trend})")
    ax.set_title(f"{v}: WY totals"); ax.set_xlabel("water year"); ax.set_ylabel("mm/yr"); ax.legend(loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "annual_totals"); plt.show()
md(pd.DataFrame({v: dict(trend=r.trend, p=round(r.p,3), tau=round(r.Tau,3),
                         sen_slope_mm_per_yr2=round(r.slope,2)) for v, r in mkres.items()}).T)
```

Precipitation is **weakly seasonal** (Walsh–Lawler seasonality index SI = 0.43, @walsh1981, i.e. moderately seasonal; monthly means range
2.6 mm/d in October to 5.1 mm/d in March) with a **double peak** (Feb–Mar frontal, July convective) and a
distinct autumn minimum. 54.9 % of days are exactly zero, 40.2 % exceed 0.1 mm and the mean wet-day
intensity is 9.8 mm — i.e. rainfall arrives in few, intense events (the 221.5 mm record day is
WY1974). There is **no significant trend** in annual P, PET or Q (Mann–Kendall [@mann1945; @kendall1975], p ≥ 0.35).

# Potential evapotranspiration PET {#sec-pet}

```{python}
#| label: fig-pet-clim
#| fig-cap: "Is PET a repeated climatology? (a) mean seasonal cycle with the ±1 SD inter-annual band and 30 individual years overplotted; (b) spread of same-day-of-year values across years; (c) PET on 15 June of each year. The inter-annual variability is large, so PET is NOT a climatology."
pet_by_doy = d.pivot_table(index="doy", columns=d.index.year, values="PET")
mu, sd = pet_by_doy.mean(axis=1), pet_by_doy.std(axis=1)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.3))
for y in range(1955, 1985): axs[0].plot(pet_by_doy.index, pet_by_doy[y], lw=.3, color="grey", alpha=.5)
axs[0].plot(mu.index, mu, color="#d62728", lw=2, label="mean over 40 yr")
axs[0].fill_between(mu.index, mu-sd, mu+sd, color="#d62728", alpha=.25, label="±1 SD (inter-annual)")
axs[0].set_xlabel("day of year"); axs[0].set_ylabel("PET (mm/d)"); axs[0].legend(); axs[0].set_title("(a) seasonal cycle")
axs[1].plot(sd.index, sd, color="k", lw=.8); axs[1].set_xlabel("day of year")
axs[1].set_ylabel("inter-annual SD (mm/d)"); axs[1].set_title("(b) same-DOY spread")
jun15 = d[(d.index.month == 6) & (d.index.day == 15)]
axs[2].plot(jun15.index.year, jun15.PET, "o-", ms=3, color="#d62728")
axs[2].set_xlabel("year"); axs[2].set_ylabel("PET on 15 June (mm/d)"); axs[2].set_title("(c) one calendar day")
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "PET_climatology_test"); plt.show()

amp_seasonal = float((mu.max()-mu.min())/2)
print(f"seasonal amplitude of the PET climatology : {amp_seasonal:.3f} mm/d")
print(f"mean same-DOY inter-annual SD             : {sd.mean():.3f} mm/d  (max {sd.max():.3f})")
print(f"ratio inter-annual SD / seasonal amplitude: {sd.mean()/amp_seasonal:.2f}")
print(f"variance explained by a smooth climatology: {1 - (sd**2).mean()/PET.var():.3f}")
print(f"corr(P, PET) daily {np.corrcoef(Pv, PETv)[0,1]:+.3f} | monthly totals "
      f"{np.corrcoef(P.resample('MS').sum(), PET.resample('MS').sum())[0,1]:+.3f}")
KEY["pet_is_climatological"] = bool(sd.mean()/amp_seasonal < 0.10)
KEY["pet_doy_interannual_sd_mm_d"] = float(sd.mean())
```

**PET is not climatological.** A pure repeated-climatology series would have a same-DOY inter-annual SD of
0; here it is 1.30 mm/d, 71 % of the seasonal amplitude (1.83 mm/d), and only ~53 % of the total PET
variance is explained by the smooth seasonal cycle. Day-to-day PET therefore carries real meteorological
information (cloudiness/temperature), which (i) justifies giving PET to ML models as a second forcing
channel rather than a deterministic function of the calendar, and (ii) means conceptual models will respond
to inter-annual PET anomalies. PET is **negatively correlated with P** (r = −0.27 daily and monthly), as
expected (rainy days are cloudy days).

## Verification of the record start date and period definition {#sec-alignment}

ISSUE-001 (evaluation window given as row indices 265:1360 vs. as the calendar window
1948-10-01…1951-09-30) was **resolved by the user on 2026-09-15**: `config/project.yaml` now uses
`periods.definition: dates`. This subsection *verifies* that resolution from the data themselves.

```{python}
#| label: fig-alignment
#| fig-cap: "Phase check. Under the assumed start 1948-10-01 (top row) the fitted annual harmonic of PET peaks on 6 July and P/Q peak in late winter-early spring — the expected Northern-Hemisphere pattern for Mississippi. Under the rejected alternative (record starts 1948-01-10, so that file rows 265:1360 would be 'Oct 1948-Sep 1951'; bottom row) PET would peak in September-October and be minimal in April, which is physically impossible."
n = len(d); t = np.arange(n)
def harmonic(y, T=365.25):
    X = np.c_[np.ones(n), np.cos(2*np.pi*t/T), np.sin(2*np.pi*t/T)]
    b = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
    amp  = float(np.hypot(b[1], b[2]))
    tpk  = float((np.arctan2(b[2], b[1])/(2*np.pi)) % 1.0 * T)     # days after row 0
    r2   = float(1 - ((y - X@b)**2).sum()/((y - y.mean())**2).sum())
    return b[0], amp, tpk, r2

H = {}
for v, y in [("P", Pv), ("PET", PETv), ("Q", Qv)]:
    H[v] = harmonic(y)
start_H1 = pd.Timestamp("1948-10-01")                    # active hypothesis (config)
start_H2 = start_H1 - pd.Timedelta(days=265)             # rows 265:1360 == Oct 1948 .. Sep 1951
rows_align = []
for v in ["P","PET","Q"]:
    m, amp, tpk, r2 = H[v]
    rows_align.append(dict(variable=v, mean=round(m,3), amplitude=round(amp,3), R2=round(r2,3),
                           peak_row=round(tpk,1),
                           peak_date_H1=(start_H1+pd.Timedelta(days=round(tpk))).strftime("%d %b"),
                           peak_date_H2=(start_H2+pd.Timedelta(days=round(tpk))).strftime("%d %b")))
align = pd.DataFrame(rows_align).set_index("variable")

fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(13, 5.6))
for j, (v, c) in enumerate(zip(["P","PET","Q"], ["#1f77b4","#d62728","#2ca02c"])):
    for i, (st, lab) in enumerate([(start_H1, "H1: start 1948-10-01 (config)"),
                                   (start_H2, "H2: start 1948-01-10 (rejected)")]):
        idx = pd.date_range(st, periods=n, freq="D")
        clim = pd.Series(d[v].to_numpy(), index=idx).groupby(idx.month).mean()
        axs[i, j].bar(clim.index, clim.values, color=c)
        axs[i, j].axvline(clim.idxmax(), color="k", ls="--", lw=1)
        axs[i, j].set_xticks(range(1, 13)); axs[i, j].set_xlabel("calendar month")
        axs[i, j].set_ylabel(f"{v} (mm/d)")
        axs[i, j].set_title(f"{lab}\n{v} max in month {clim.idxmax()}", fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "date_alignment_check"); plt.show()
md(align)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-alignment
print("H1 (active, `dates`): record row 0 = 1948-10-01")
print(f"   PET annual harmonic peaks {H['PET'][2]:.0f} d after row 0 = "
      f"{(start_H1+pd.Timedelta(days=round(H['PET'][2]))).strftime('%d %B')}; "
      f"monthly PET max in June ({d.groupby('month')['PET'].mean().max():.2f} mm/d), min in January "
      f"({d.groupby('month')['PET'].mean().min():.2f} mm/d)")
print(f"   Q monthly max in {d.groupby('month')['Q'].mean().idxmax()} (Feb-Apr, cool season, low PET), "
      f"min in {d.groupby('month')['Q'].mean().idxmin()} (Sep, peak PET)  -> consistent")
print("H2 (rejected): record row 0 = 1948-01-10 so that rows 265:1360 = 1948-10-01..1951-09-30")
idx2 = pd.date_range(start_H2, periods=n, freq="D")
clim2 = pd.Series(PETv, index=idx2).groupby(idx2.month).mean()
import calendar
print(f"   PET monthly climatology would peak in {calendar.month_name[int(clim2.idxmax())]} "
      f"and be minimal in {calendar.month_name[int(clim2.idxmin())]}; the fitted harmonic would peak on "
      f"{(start_H2+pd.Timedelta(days=round(H['PET'][2]))).strftime('%d %B')}")
print(f"   -> physically impossible in the Northern Hemisphere; H2 rejected.")
print()
print("Superseded index window, evaluated under H1:")
print(f"   rows 265:1360  = {d.index[265].date()} .. {d.index[1359].date()}   (not Oct 1948-Sep 1951)")
print(f"   rows 357:1360  = {d.index[357].date()} .. {d.index[1359].date()}   (metric sub-window)")
print("Active window (config/project.yaml, periods.definition = dates):")
for k in ["evaluation run","evaluation warm-up","evaluation metric","calibration run",
          "calibration warm-up","calibration metric","internal train","internal validation"]:
    a, b = WIN[k]; s = win(k)
    print(f"   {k:20s} {a} .. {b}  = rows {int(s['row'].iloc[0]):5d}:{int(s['row'].iloc[-1])+1:5d}  n={len(s):5d}")
```

**Conclusion.** Three independent lines of evidence fix row 0 at 1948-10-01:

1. **PET phase** — the fitted annual harmonic (R² = 0.46) peaks 278 days after row 0. Under H1 that is
   **6 July**, and the monthly climatology maximum is June (4.65 mm/d) with a January minimum (1.03 mm/d):
   textbook Northern-Hemisphere. Under H2 the same harmonic peak falls on **14 October** (monthly maximum in
   September–October) with an **April minimum** — evaporative demand highest in autumn and lowest in spring,
   which is impossible for Mississippi.
2. **Q/P phase** — Q peaks in Feb–Apr and is minimal in September, the classic humid-subtropical pattern
   driven by the PET cycle (P itself is only weakly seasonal); annual Q maxima occur in Dec–May in 38 of
   40 water years.
3. **Record length** — 14,610 days = exactly 40 water years including 10 leap days, which only closes for
   an Oct-1 start.

This confirms `periods.definition: dates`. The superseded row window 265:1360 corresponds to
**1949-06-23 … 1952-06-21** — a window that begins in mid-summer and does not match the benchmark study's
verbatim description ("Oct 1, 1948 through Sept 30, 1951", first three months as warm-up, metrics from
1 Jan 1949). Since that study used the identical file (md5 `a5c922ef2b009a63ba6089172fd90cc2`), the
row-index form was simply a mis-translation of the same calendar window. **No change to
`config/project.yaml` is needed or made here.**

Daily flow spans nearly three orders of magnitude (0.069–64.0 mm/d) with skewness 6.8 and kurtosis 77.
In log space the distribution is close to normal (panel b), which is the key argument for a
variance-stabilising transform in any least-squares objective (@sec-implications, input to a04).
The hydrograph is **moderately flashy** (Richards–Baker index 0.32, @baker2004) and dominated by falling limbs (64.6 % of
days), with a median recession ratio of 0.91 per day.

# Joint analysis and hydrological signatures {#sec-signatures}

## Baseflow separation [@lyne1979; @eckhardt2005]

```{python}
#| label: fig-baseflow
#| fig-cap: "Lyne-Hollick baseflow separation [@lyne1979; @nathan1990] (alpha = 0.925, 3 passes) for two contrasting water years; the shaded area is baseflow."
def lyne_hollick(q, a=0.925, passes=3):
    b = q.copy()
    for p in range(passes):
        y = b[::-1] if p % 2 else b
        f = np.zeros_like(y); f[0] = y[0]
        for i in range(1, len(y)):
            f[i] = a*f[i-1] + (1+a)/2*(y[i]-y[i-1])
        bf = np.minimum(y, y - np.maximum(f, 0))
        b = bf[::-1] if p % 2 else bf
    return np.clip(b, 0, q)

bf = lyne_hollick(Qv); qf = Qv - bf
BFI_LH = float(bf.sum()/Qv.sum())
d["bf"] = bf
bfi_wy = d.groupby("wy").apply(lambda s: s.bf.sum()/s.Q.sum()).loc[1949:1988]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 3.2), sharey=True)
for ax, wy in zip(axs, [1980, 1963]):
    s = d[d.wy == wy]
    ax.fill_between(s.index, 0, s.bf, color="#9edae5", label="baseflow (LH)")
    ax.plot(s.index, s.Q, color="#2ca02c", lw=.8, label="Q")
    ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_ylabel("Q (mm/d)")
    ax.set_title(f"WY{wy} — BFI = {bfi_wy[wy]:.2f} ({'wettest' if wy==1980 else 'driest'} year)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "baseflow"); plt.show()
print(f"BFI Lyne-Hollick (alpha=0.925, 3 passes, whole record): {BFI_LH:.3f}")
print(f"BFI per water year: mean {bfi_wy.mean():.3f}, range {bfi_wy.min():.3f} (WY{bfi_wy.idxmin()}) - {bfi_wy.max():.3f} (WY{bfi_wy.idxmax()})")
```

## Recession analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-recession
#| fig-cap: "Recession behaviour. (a) Brutsaert-Nieber [@brutsaert1977] plot -dQ/dt vs Q on 442 rainless recession segments of >=5 days, with the fitted power law; (b) distribution of segment-wise recession constants k = exp(slope of log Q)."
rec_mask = np.r_[False, np.diff(Qv) < 0] & (Pv < 0.1)
runs, c = [], 0
for i, m in enumerate(rec_mask):
    if m: c += 1
    else:
        if c >= 5: runs.append((i-c, i))
        c = 0
ks, Qm, dQm = [], [], []
for a_, b_ in runs:
    seg = Qv[a_-1:b_]
    ks.append(np.exp(np.polyfit(np.arange(len(seg)), np.log(seg), 1)[0]))
    Qm.append((seg[:-1]+seg[1:])/2); dQm.append(-np.diff(seg))
ks = np.array(ks); Qm = np.concatenate(Qm); dQm = np.concatenate(dQm)
ok = dQm > 0
bBN, aBN = np.polyfit(np.log(Qm[ok]), np.log(dQm[ok]), 1)
k_med = float(np.median(ks)); tau = -1/np.log(k_med)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.4))
axs[0].loglog(Qm[ok], dQm[ok], ".", ms=2, alpha=.3, color="#2ca02c")
xx = np.logspace(np.log10(Qm[ok].min()), np.log10(Qm[ok].max()), 50)
axs[0].loglog(xx, np.exp(aBN)*xx**bBN, "k-", lw=1.5, label=f"-dQ/dt = {np.exp(aBN):.3f} Q^{bBN:.2f}")
axs[0].set_xlabel("Q (mm/d)"); axs[0].set_ylabel("-dQ/dt (mm/d²)"); axs[0].legend(); axs[0].set_title("(a) Brutsaert-Nieber")
axs[1].hist(ks, bins=40, color="#2ca02c")
axs[1].axvline(k_med, color="k", ls="--", label=f"median k = {k_med:.3f}\n(tau = {tau:.1f} d)")
axs[1].set_xlabel("segment recession constant k (1/d)"); axs[1].legend(); axs[1].set_title("(b) recession constants")
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "recession"); plt.show()
print(f"{len(runs)} rainless recession segments >=5 d ({sum(b_-a_ for a_,b_ in runs)} days, "
      f"{100*sum(b_-a_ for a_,b_ in runs)/len(d):.1f}% of the record)")
print(f"master recession constant k = {k_med:.4f} /d  ->  residence time tau = {tau:.1f} d")
print(f"Brutsaert-Nieber exponent b = {bBN:.2f} (b=1 linear reservoir, b~1.5 Boussinesq) , a = {np.exp(aBN):.3f}")
def eckhardt(q, a, BFImax):
    b = np.empty_like(q); b[0] = q[0]*BFImax
    for i in range(1, len(q)):
        b[i] = min(((1-BFImax)*a*b[i-1] + (1-a)*BFImax*q[i])/(1-a*BFImax), q[i])
    return b
BFI_E = {bm: float(eckhardt(Qv, k_med, bm).sum()/Qv.sum()) for bm in (0.50, 0.80)}
print(f"BFI Eckhardt (a={k_med:.3f}): BFImax=0.50 -> {BFI_E[0.50]:.3f} ; BFImax=0.80 -> {BFI_E[0.80]:.3f}")
KEY["bfi_lyne_hollick"] = BFI_LH; KEY["bfi_eckhardt_bfimax080"] = BFI_E[0.80]
KEY["recession_k"] = k_med; KEY["recession_tau_days"] = float(tau); KEY["bn_exponent_b"] = float(bBN)
```

Roughly 40 % of the annual flow volume is baseflow (Lyne–Hollick 0.41; Eckhardt 0.45 with BFImax = 0.5,
0.71 with the sandy-aquifer value BFImax = 0.8). The Brutsaert–Nieber exponent b = 1.68 is **clearly
non-linear** (> 1): recession is faster at high flow, which a single linear reservoir cannot reproduce —
two parallel stores (or a non-linear store) are needed.

## Memory: autocorrelation and P→Q lag

```{python}
#| label: fig-memory
#| fig-cap: "Catchment memory. (a) autocorrelation of Q and log Q up to 120 days; (b) cross-correlation of P with Q and with dQ/dt: the flow *change* peaks at lag 1 day, the flow *level* at lag 3 days; (c) R² of a linear model of Q on the last L days of P as a function of L."
lags = np.arange(0, 121)
acq  = np.array([Q.autocorr(l) for l in lags])
aclq = np.array([np.log(Q).autocorr(l) for l in lags])
xl   = np.arange(0, 31)
xcQ  = np.array([np.corrcoef(Pv[:len(Pv)-l], Qv[l:])[0,1] for l in xl])
dQv  = np.r_[0, np.diff(Qv)]
xcdQ = np.array([np.corrcoef(Pv[:len(Pv)-l], dQv[l:])[0,1] for l in xl])
Ls   = [5,10,20,30,60,90,120,180,365]
r2L  = []
for L in Ls:
    X = np.column_stack([np.r_[np.zeros(k), Pv[:len(Pv)-k]] for k in range(L)] + [np.ones(len(Pv))])
    b = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Qv, rcond=None)[0]
    r2L.append(1 - ((Qv - X@b)**2).sum()/((Qv-Qv.mean())**2).sum())
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.3))
axs[0].plot(lags, acq, label="Q"); axs[0].plot(lags, aclq, label="log Q")
axs[0].axhline(np.exp(-1), color="grey", ls=":"); axs[0].set_xlabel("lag (d)"); axs[0].set_ylabel("ACF")
axs[0].legend(); axs[0].set_title("(a) autocorrelation")
axs[1].plot(xl, xcQ, "o-", ms=3, label="corr(P_t, Q_t+l)")
axs[1].plot(xl, xcdQ, "s-", ms=3, label="corr(P_t, dQ_t+l)")
axs[1].axhline(0, color="k", lw=.5); axs[1].set_xlabel("lag l (d)"); axs[1].legend(); axs[1].set_title("(b) P -> Q lag")
axs[2].plot(Ls, r2L, "o-"); axs[2].set_xscale("log"); axs[2].set_xlabel("input window length L (d)")
axs[2].set_ylabel("R² of linear P-lag model"); axs[2].set_title("(c) how much history matters")
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "memory"); plt.show()
efold_q  = int(np.argmax(acq  < np.exp(-1)))
efold_lq = int(np.argmax(aclq < np.exp(-1)))
print(f"ACF(Q)   lag1 {acq[1]:.3f}  lag3 {acq[3]:.3f}  lag7 {acq[7]:.3f}  lag30 {acq[30]:.3f}  e-folding {efold_q} d")
print(f"ACF(logQ) lag1 {aclq[1]:.3f} lag7 {aclq[7]:.3f} lag30 {aclq[30]:.3f} lag90 {aclq[90]:.3f} e-folding {efold_lq} d")
print(f"peak cross-correlation P->Q at lag {int(xl[np.argmax(xcQ)])} d (r={xcQ.max():.3f}); "
      f"P->dQ/dt at lag {int(xl[np.argmax(xcdQ)])} d (r={xcdQ.max():.3f})")
print("linear P-lag model R²:", {L: round(r,3) for L, r in zip(Ls, r2L)})
KEY["lag_peak_xcorr_days"]   = int(xl[np.argmax(xcQ)])
KEY["lag_response_onset_days"]= int(xl[np.argmax(xcdQ)])
KEY["acf_logQ_efolding_days"]= efold_lq
KEY["acf_Q_lag1"]            = float(acq[1])
```

## Event runoff coefficients {#sec-events}

```{python}
#| label: fig-events
#| fig-cap: "Runoff coefficients of 31 isolated rainfall events (>=20 mm after >=5 dry days, followed by 10 quiet days). The event response varies by two orders of magnitude and increases with antecedent wetness (antecedent Q) and with event size — direct evidence of threshold/nonlinear runoff generation."
events, i = [], 6
while i < len(Pv) - 16:
    if Pv[i] >= 20 and Pv[i-5:i].sum() < 2:
        L = 1
        while L < 3 and Pv[i+L] >= 5: L += 1
        if Pv[i+L:i+L+10].sum() < 5:
            pe = Pv[i:i+L].sum(); qe = qf[i:i+L+10].sum()
            events.append(dict(date=d.index[i], dur=L, P_mm=pe, Qdir_mm=qe, RC=qe/pe, Q_ante=Qv[i-1],
                               month=d.index[i].month))
            i += L + 10; continue
    i += 1
EV = pd.DataFrame(events)
EV["season"] = np.where(EV.month.isin([11,12,1,2,3,4]), "cool (Nov-Apr)", "warm (May-Oct)")
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.2))
sc = axs[0].scatter(EV.Q_ante, EV.RC, c=EV.P_mm, cmap="viridis", s=30)
axs[0].set_xscale("log"); axs[0].set_xlabel("antecedent Q (mm/d)"); axs[0].set_ylabel("runoff coefficient (-)")
plt.colorbar(sc, ax=axs[0], label="event P (mm)"); axs[0].set_title(f"(a) RC vs antecedent flow (r={EV.RC.corr(EV.Q_ante):.2f})")
axs[1].scatter(EV.P_mm, EV.RC, c="#1f77b4", s=30); axs[1].set_xlabel("event P (mm)")
axs[1].set_ylabel("RC (-)"); axs[1].set_title(f"(b) RC vs event depth (r={EV.RC.corr(EV.P_mm):.2f})")
sns.boxplot(data=EV, x="season", y="RC", ax=axs[2], color="#1f77b4", linewidth=.8)
axs[2].set_title("(c) seasonal contrast")
fig.tight_layout(); save(fig, "event_runoff_coefficients"); plt.show()
print(f"n isolated events = {len(EV)}; RC: min {EV.RC.min():.3f}, median {EV.RC.median():.3f}, "
      f"mean {EV.RC.mean():.3f}, max {EV.RC.max():.3f}")
md(EV.groupby("season")["RC"].agg(["count","mean","median","min","max"]).round(3))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-qc
# 1) physically impossible annual balances
qc = {}
qc["water years with Q > P"] = int((ann.Q > ann.P).sum())
qc["water years with runoff ratio > 0.8"] = int((ann.RR > 0.8).sum())
qc["water years with runoff ratio < 0.15"] = int((ann.RR < 0.15).sum())
# 2) flow rises without rain
rise_noP = (dQv > 0.5) & (P.rolling(3).sum().fillna(0).to_numpy() < 1.0)
qc["days with dQ > 0.5 mm/d and 3-day P < 1 mm"] = int(rise_noP.sum())
# 3) large rain without response
bigP = Pv > 25
resp = np.array([dQv[i+1:i+4].max() if i+4 < len(dQv) else 0 for i in np.where(bigP)[0]])
qc["days with P > 25 mm"] = int(bigP.sum())
qc["...of which no response within 3 d (dQ < 0.1 mm/d)"] = int((resp < 0.1).sum())
# 4) timing offset diagnostics
qc["corr(P_t, dQ_t)"]   = float(np.corrcoef(Pv, dQv)[0,1])
qc["corr(P_t, dQ_t+1)"] = float(np.corrcoef(Pv[:-1], dQv[1:])[0,1])
qc["corr(P_t, dQ_t+2)"] = float(np.corrcoef(Pv[:-2], dQv[2:])[0,1])
md(pd.Series(qc, name="value").to_frame())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-stationarity
def pettitt(x):
    n = len(x); r = np.argsort(np.argsort(x)) + 1
    U = np.array([2*r[:k].sum() - k*(n+1) for k in range(1, n+1)])
    K = int(np.abs(U).max()); k = int(np.abs(U).argmax())
    p = float(min(2*np.exp(-6*K**2/(n**3 + n**2)), 1.0))
    return k, K, p
rows = []
for v in ["P","PET","Q"]:
    k, K, p = pettitt(ann[v].to_numpy())
    rows.append(dict(variable=v, change_point_after=f"WY{ann.index[k]}", K=K, p_value=round(p,3),
                     significant_5pct=p < 0.05))
dec = d.assign(decade=(d.index.year//10)*10).groupby("decade")[["P","PET","Q"]].mean()*365.25
md(pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("variable"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-decades
md(dec.round(0).rename(columns=lambda c: f"{c} (mm/yr)"))
```

**QC verdict.** The record passes every check:

* no year has Q > P; runoff ratios stay within 0.19–0.60, all physically sensible;
* the 33 days with a rise of >0.5 mm/d and almost no rain in the preceding 3 days were inspected
  individually — every one of them follows a large multi-day storm 3–6 days earlier (e.g. 1950-05-05 with
  107 mm in the previous 5 days) and is therefore a **routing delay, not an inconsistency**;
* 32 of 650 days with P > 25 mm produce no flow response within 3 days; these occur almost exclusively in
  summer at very low antecedent flow, i.e. they are genuine storage-deficit events, not data errors;
* the P→Q timing is internally consistent: corr(P_t, dQ_t) = 0.15 but corr(P_t, dQ_{t+1}) = 0.50, so the
  response starts on the day of the storm and peaks on the following day. **No 1-day offset correction is
  warranted** (shifting P by one day would degrade the same-day correlation to zero);
* Pettitt tests [@pettitt1979] find no significant change point in annual P, PET or Q (p ≥ 0.35); the double-mass curve has
  no break (maximum deviation 729 mm = 3.6 % of cumulative Q, a smooth wet/dry oscillation).
* Decadal means show the 1950s as the driest decade (P 1,295 mm/yr, Q 393 mm/yr) and the 1970s as the
  wettest (P 1,574 mm/yr, Q 604 mm/yr) — climate variability, not inhomogeneity.

```{python}
def period_stats(name):
    s = win(name)
    return pd.Series({
        "start": s.index[0].date(), "end": s.index[-1].date(),
        "rows": f"{int(s['row'].iloc[0])}:{int(s['row'].iloc[-1])+1}", "n days": len(s),
        "P (mm/yr)": s.P.mean()*365.25, "PET (mm/yr)": s.PET.mean()*365.25, "Q (mm/yr)": s.Q.mean()*365.25,
        "runoff ratio": s.Q.sum()/s.P.sum(),
        "Q mean": s.Q.mean(), "Q median": s.Q.median(), "Q p95": s.Q.quantile(.95),
        "Q p99": s.Q.quantile(.99), "Q max": s.Q.max(), "Q min": s.Q.min(),
        "Q sd": s.Q.std(), "Q skew": s.Q.skew(),
        "P zero days (%)": 100*(s.P == 0).mean(), "P max": s.P.max(),
        "peaks/yr (Q>9*Q50_all)": (np.diff(np.r_[0,(s.Q > 9*Q50).astype(int)]) == 1).sum()/(len(s)/365.25),
    })
names = ["evaluation metric", "calibration metric", "internal train", "internal validation"]
PT = pd.DataFrame({n: period_stats(n) for n in names})
md(PT.map(lambda v: round(v, 3) if isinstance(v, float) else v))
```

**Reading of the table.** The evaluation window is *inside* the calibration range but in its wet tail:
the evaluation metric period has 1.29× the mean flow, 1.10× the mean P and a runoff ratio of 0.41 against
0.35 for calibration. 1.7 % of evaluation days exceed the calibration Q99 (1.7× the expected 1 %), and
6.6 % exceed the calibration Q95. No evaluation day exceeds the calibration maximum (45.9 vs 64.0 mm/d),
so **no strict extrapolation of the flow magnitude is required** — but models that trade high-flow bias for
low-flow accuracy during calibration will be penalised on this wetter window. WY1949 is the wettest water
year of the entire record (2,057 mm P, rank 1/40; 956 mm Q, rank 2/40).
Internal train and internal validation are, by contrast, very similar to each other (mean Q 1.373 vs
1.272 mm/d, runoff ratio 0.352 vs 0.324), so the internal split is a fair early-stopping/ranking device.

# Implications for downstream agents {#sec-implications}

**a03 (model proposer) — processes, memory, nonlinearity**

* Two storage time scales are mandatory: a fast one (event response peaks 1–3 d after rain,
  Richards–Baker 0.32) and a slow one (BFI 0.41, log-Q ACF e-folding 48 d, recession τ ≈ 9 d for the
  intermediate store and much longer tails).
* Recession is **non-linear** (Brutsaert–Nieber b = 1.68 ≠ 1): prefer a non-linear lower zone
  (SAC-SMA/HBV-style) or ≥2 parallel linear reservoirs (HYMOD's quick tanks + slow tank).
* Runoff generation is strongly **threshold-controlled**: event runoff coefficients span 0.004–0.45 and
  scale with antecedent flow (r = 0.57) → a saturation-excess / variable-contributing-area formulation
  (Probability-Distributed soil Moisture, as in HYMOD, or SAC-SMA's tension stores) is the natural choice.
* Seasonality comes from PET, not P: mean P varies 2.6–5.1 mm/d over the year while mean Q varies
  0.38–2.88 mm/d. Models must reproduce the summer evaporative shutdown (JJA: P 330 mm, PET 409 mm,
  Q 42 mm) — no snow processes are needed in south Mississippi.
* Long memory: a linear model on the last L days of P keeps improving to L ≈ 365 (R² 0.59 → 0.65).
  **Recommended LSTM sequence length 180–365 days [cf. @kratzert2018] (use 365 if memory allows, 180 as a cheap default);
  conceptual warm-up ≥ 365 days** — which is what the calibration window already provides
  (1951-10-01…1952-09-30). Note the evaluation warm-up prescribed by the protocol is only 92 days
  (Oct–Dec 1948), so models should be initialised from a plausible near-median storage state rather than
  from empty stores.
* PET is **not** climatological (same-DOY inter-annual SD 1.30 mm/d): feed the actual PET series, do not
  replace it with a seasonal curve.

**a04 (metrics advisor) — distribution and objective transformation**

* Daily Q: skewness 6.8, kurtosis 77, Q5/Q95 = 47, log-normal-shaped in log space; the wettest 1 % of
  days carry 16 % and the wettest 5 % carry 40 % of the total flow volume. Untransformed squared errors (NSE/KGE on Q) are dominated by ~20 flood days
  per year.
* Q is **strictly positive** (min 0.069 mm/d) → log, sqrt and Box-Cox transforms need **no offset**;
  sensible complements to the mandated KGE/NSE during development are KGE on log Q or sqrt Q, or a
  split KGE / FDC-signature diagnostics [@yilmaz2008]. Final reporting stays KGE + NSE on untransformed Q, per `config/project.yaml`.
* Calibration-period moments for the KGE β/α terms: mean 1.3533 mm/d, sd 2.8511 mm/d.

**a05–a09 (model builders) — units and practicalities**

* All three series are mm/day; no unit conversion is needed anywhere. Basin area ≈ 1,950 km² if a discharge
  in m³/s is ever required (1 mm/d = 22.57 m³/s).
* P has 54.9 % exact zeros; Q has **no** zeros and no NaN → no special missing-value or zero-flow handling.
* Never derive scaling constants from anything but @sec-scaling.

**a10 (optimisation advisor) — response-surface expectations**

* 13,149 calibration days with a heavy-tailed target: the objective surface for untransformed NSE/KGE is
  dominated by a handful of flood years (WY1961, WY1974, WY1980) and is therefore rough;
  global search (SCE-UA/DE) rather than local gradient descent is advised, consistent with the fact that
  this exact data set is the SCE-UA benchmark [@duan1992].
* Strong parameter interaction is expected between the fast/slow partition (BFI ≈ 0.41) and the recession
  constants (k ≈ 0.90).

**a16 (evaluator) — risks**

* The evaluation window is the **wettest** part of the record (Q mean ratio 1.29, WY1949 the wettest year).
  A model calibrated on 1952–1988 will most likely show a positive α and a slight negative β bias there;
  report the KGE decomposition, not just the total.
* The evaluation warm-up is only 92 days — differences between models in initial-state handling will be
  visible in Jan–Mar 1949. Warm-up rows are not scored (metric starts 1949-01-01).

```{python}
print(f"written : {out.relative_to(ROOT)}  ({out.stat().st_size/1e3:.1f} kB)")
print(f"shape   : {chk.shape}, columns {list(chk.columns)}, index {chk.index[0].date()}..{chk.index[-1].date()}")
print(f"identical to load_data(): {chk.equals(df)}")
```

The processed file is a byte-faithful copy of what `src.common.data.load_data()` returns (no derived
columns, no filtering) — it exists so downstream agents can load the record without re-parsing the ASCII
file, but **the canonical access path remains `src/common/data.py`**.
